scored_papers.title: A bright source of high-dimensional spatially entangled photon pairs based on beam-like Type-II SPDC
scored_papers.abstract: Bright sources of high-dimensional spatially entangled photon pairs are increasingly required for the rapid advancement of quantum technologies. However, simultaneously achieving high brightness and high-dimensional spatial entanglement through spontaneous parametric down-conversion (SPDC) remains challenging. Here, we demonstrate a bright source of high-dimensional spatially entangled photon pairs using beam-like Type-II SPDC in a $\beta$-barium borate crystal. Compared with a conventional collinear Type-I source, it exhibits a $\sim$1.56-fold enhancement in the detected single-photon count rate and a $\sim$1.45-fold enhancement in the coincidence count rate. Measurements of position correlations and momentum anti-correlations certify at least 62-dimensional spatial entanglement within a 121-dimensional basis. These correlations are further exploited to demonstrate quantum imaging in both the position and momentum domains. These characteristics make the source a practical resource for high-dimensional photonic quantum technologies.

scored_papers.summary: 📊 BBO 結晶のビーム状 Type-II SPDC で、従来の共線 Type-I 源比で単一光子計数約1.56倍・同時計数約1.45倍。121次元基底中62次元以上の空間もつれを認証し、位置・運動量両領域の量子イメージングも実証。

scored_papers.title: Why do single photons produce interference fringes? The phase of a mode and the phase of a state
scored_papers.abstract: If the phase of a photon-number state is completely undetermined, how can single photons, sent one at a time through a two-slit apparatus, build up interference fringes? These lecture notes answer this question from first principles. Starting from Maxwell's equations, we expand the field in vector modes, quantize it, and introduce the quantity measured by a photodetector. We then show that the word ``phase'' refers to two different things: the phase of a mode, fixed by the optical setup, and the phase of the quantum state that excites the mode. Only the first determines the fringes. All calculations are given in full, and problems with solutions are included.
scored_papers.reason: 💡🌊🔦✨ 位相が不定な光子数状態の単一光子が、なぜ二重スリットで干渉縞を作るのか！縞を決めるのはモードの位相で状態の位相ではない、と第一原理から解く講義ノート🎯
scored_papers.summary: 📖 Maxwell 方程式からベクトルモード展開・量子化・光検出器の測定量まで導出し、「位相」をモードの位相（光学系で固定）と状態の位相に分ける。縞を決めるのは前者のみ。全計算と演習付き。

scored_papers.title: Direct generation of N00N states with layered semiconductors
scored_papers.abstract: Photonic N00N states enable phase sensing beyond the classical limit, but their generation conventionally relies on interferometric manipulation of photons using bulk optical components. Here we demonstrate the direct generation of a family of tunable two-photon polarization N00N states from a subwavelength-thick 3R-MoS2 flake. For propagation along the optic axis, the in-plane crystal symmetry allows all symmetry permitted spontaneous parametric down-conversion pathway to interfere coherently, while the large second-order nonlinearity provides sufficient brightness at submicrometer thickness without phase matching. The pump polarization sets the basis of the N00N state or equivalently a two-photon Holland-Burnett state without altering its structure or the generation efficiency. The biphotons are highly indistinguishable, reach high fidelity with the target state across a wide range of pump polarizations, and show two-photon interference fringes with visibilities above the threshold for the postselected phase supersensitivity. Our theoretical analysis further indicates that, in the ideal single-mode limit, the same interaction would yield higher-order Holland-Burnett states. By eliminating interferometric stages, our results establish a compact, pump-programmable source for quantum-enhanced polarization interferometry
